clean.description: The modulo operation for wrapping can produce incorrect results: when HighlightedIndex is -1 and delta is negative, ((-1 + (-1)) % count + count) % count evaluates to ((-2 % count) + count) % count, which gives count - 2 instead of count - 1, skipping the last entry.

The height calculation counts dividers for all items with StartsGroup=true, but StartsGroup is only set to true when i > 0 (line 91), so the first item never has a divider. However, the Measure function doesn't account for this logic and will overcount dividers if the first item has StartsGroup set externally.

Row height comes only from the unscaled icon plus scaled padding and ignores the text height (DebugFont.LineHeight * scale), so at larger UI scales the label can be taller than its row and overlap neighbouring rows and dividers.

Moving the pointer off every entry keeps the old highlight, so a disabled entry's reason tooltip stays visible at the pointer even when it is outside the menu or over another area, not only while that entry is hovered.

Because Hover keeps the previous highlight when the pointer leaves an entry, the disabled-reason tooltip stays visible (anchored to the pointer, possibly outside the menu) after the pointer has moved off the disabled entry, rather than only while hovering it.
Hovering away from a disabled entry onto menu padding, a divider, or outside the menu does not clear the highlight, so its disabled-reason tooltip remains visible when the entry is no longer hovered.
